subtopics.title: Question Walk — Newton's Laws on an Incline

questions.question: For the 8 kg block on the 30° incline, the weight component along the slope is:
With 80 N applied up the slope, 39,2 N of weight component and 10 N of friction opposing, the acceleration is:
The block moves UP the slope, so kinetic friction acts:
options: Down the slope, opposing the motion
Up the slope, helping the applied force

questions.question: A complete free-body diagram for this block shows:
options: Only the applied force and friction
Weight, normal force and friction only
The resultant force as a single arrow
Weight, normal force, applied force and friction, all labelled with directions

subtopics.title: Question Walk — Momentum, Impulse and the Collision

questions.question: A 5 kg trolley at 4 m·s⁻¹ couples with a stationary 3 kg trolley. The combined velocity is:
Kinetic energy drops from 40 J to 25 J in the coupling. The collision is:
options: Elastic, because the trolleys moved together
Inelastic, because kinetic energy was not conserved

questions.question: The impulse on trolley B (3 kg, from rest to 2,5 m·s⁻¹) has magnitude:
Conservation of linear momentum applies to the collision because the system is:
options: Isolated — the net external force on it is zero

questions.question: A ball leaves the ground upward at 19,6 m·s⁻¹. It reaches the top after:
Its maximum height is:
At t = 3 s the ball's velocity is minus 9,8 m·s⁻¹, which means:
options: 9,8 m·s⁻¹ downward — it is already descending
The calculation is wrong; speed cannot be negative

questions.question: The velocity-time graph for the whole flight is:
options: Two separate line segments meeting at the top
One straight line of gradient −9,8, from +19,6 to −19,6, crossing zero at 2 s

subtopics.title: Question Walk — Work, Energy and Power

questions.question: The 20 kg crate: net force 70 N over 5 m. The net work done is:
From Wnet = ΔEk, 350 = ½ × 20 × v², the final speed is:
The motor lifting 300 kg through 12 m at constant speed in 20 s delivers:
When a question says 'using energy methods', reaching for equations of motion instead:
options: Is fine — any correct method scores fully
Is required for the graph mark
Risks the method marks — the instruction is binding

questions.question: Ambulance at 30 m·s⁻¹ approaching, siren 800 Hz, sound speed 340 m·s⁻¹. The listener hears about:
The sign decision in the denominator follows from the physics:
options: Approach must raise the frequency, so the denominator must shrink — subtract

questions.question: After the ambulance passes, the observed frequency of about 735,14 Hz is:
options: Below the source frequency, as recession demands

questions.question: A medical application of the Doppler effect is:
options: Ultrasound measurement of blood flow or foetal heartbeat

subtopics.title: Question Walk — The Circuit with Internal Resistance

questions.question: Two 8 Ω resistors in parallel, in series with 5 Ω, plus internal resistance 1 Ω. Total circuit resistance:
With emf 20 V and total resistance 10 Ω, the terminal voltage under the 2 A load is:
The voltage across the parallel pair is 8 V, so each 8 Ω branch carries:
The power dissipated in the 5 Ω resistor carrying 2 A is:
The energy of a 400 nm photon, using E = hc/λ, is about:
With work function 3,68 × 10⁻¹⁹ J, the maximum kinetic energy of a photoelectron is about:
The trap in this calculation is usually:
options: Adding instead of subtracting the work function
Forgetting to convert 400 nm to metres before substituting

questions.question: If the light's intensity is doubled, the maximum kinetic energy of each photoelectron:
options: Stays unchanged — intensity sets photon count, not photon energy
